state.graph: Within one immutable population generation every principal has one immutable integer rank. Every accepted directed group-membership edge cites the exact same generation and immutable accepted endpoint identities, and must go from a lower rank to a higher rank. An observed edge that fails stays preserved as a rejected observation, and no complete-population assertion follows from successful individual edge checks.
state.review: Each account-entitlement review item owns its own decision and close. A report displays each item it has observed and a source-consumption checkpoint. The list can lag and can omit an item whose opening is not in the report. There is no authoritative expected-item universe. A user action ID groups independently delivered item requests but retains no server-side selected-item roster.
state.races: An actor sends decisions with operation IDs. Reusing the same ID with different intent is refused; exact retries return the original outcome. A timeout alone is not a final outcome. Membership and delegation authority may be revoked concurrently on other streams.

rank_cycle.instructions: Under graph, can accepted edges contain a directed cycle if every accepted edge strictly increases its immutable rank?

rank_dag.instructions: Could an acyclic observed graph have an edge rejected solely because its supplied immutable ranks place that edge in decreasing order?

rank_complete.instructions: Do valid ranks for all edges the system happened to examine prove it examined every observed edge?

rank_concurrent.instructions: If immutable same-generation ranks are proven for both endpoints, can two concurrent individually rank-increasing edges create a directed cycle?

rank_ref_change.instructions: If an endpoint rank could change after edge validation, would earlier rank-increasing checks necessarily still imply the currently accepted edges are acyclic?

report_complete.instructions: Does a report showing every item it has observed as closed prove every required item has closed?

checkpoint_complete.instructions: Does a report source checkpoint alone prove all required review items were created and observed?

group_exact.instructions: Does grouping received item commands under a user action ID prove that the server received every item the user intended to select?

unknown_success.instructions: Does a timeout alone prove an item decision was accepted?

revoke_race.instructions: Does a membership or delegation check on a separate stream before a decision commit, by itself, prevent the decision from committing after a concurrent revocation?

closed_item.instructions: If a review item owns one stream and atomically refuses all changes after closure, can another item be changed without changing that closed item?
